status_definitions.exact: DefenseClaw matches the pinned upstream detection boundary under the same ID.
status_definitions.equivalent: The capability is implemented under one or more established DefenseClaw IDs.
status_definitions.partial: A deliberately narrower, fact-proven subset is implemented to preserve precision.
status_definitions.deferred: Required authenticated context or lifecycle facts are not currently available.

related_prs.573: Reimplement only fact-proven Git metadata writes and container-runtime socket mounts; do not import raw-input regex or global Unicode decoding.
related_prs.525: Handle archive-to-upload data flow in a separate schema-expanding PR; do not import standalone HIGH upload rules or approximate artifact correlation.

rules.rationale: The fixed chain exists, but its first step remains dormant until an authenticated guardrail state transition is available.
The ordered chain exists with bounded correlation windows and fact-proven runtime bypasses; unsupported runtimes such as opencode are excluded.
The ordered chain exists with bounded correlation windows and exact privilege operations; ambiguous split chroot option forms are excluded.
The ordered chain requires supported secret-manager reads followed by typed external uploads within a bounded window, excluding unproven text-only egress.
The ordered chain requires a supported sensitive-path read followed by typed external upload within a bounded window, excluding variable-path and text-only egress.
The ordered chain requires fixed workload-token paths and exact workload-exec shapes within a bounded window; variable paths and ambiguous global options are excluded.
ActionFacts proves supported Claude, Codex, and Gemini bypass modes; opencode and ambiguous interactive invocation forms are excluded.
The established recursive-delete owner requires a proven delete operation and critical resolved target.
DefenseClaw deliberately narrows this to fact-proven fetch stdout flowing directly into a stdin interpreter.
DefenseClaw deliberately narrows this to portable, fact-proven decode output flowing directly into a stdin interpreter.
DefenseClaw splits reverse-shell mechanisms into stable operator-facing IDs.
The owner requires an exact reverse-forward option and external peer; space-separated option values and non-external destinations are excluded.
The established upload owner requires a sensitive file flow to an external destination.
Coverage is intentionally limited to exact resolver execution with known static substitution sources; arbitrary nested commands are excluded.
Existing owners cover environment capture flowing to an external upload.
The owner requires a proven sensitive filesystem read flowing directly into an external upload; co-occurrence without data flow is excluded.
The owner covers direct and selected wrapper-based miner launches; unmodeled wrappers such as taskset are excluded.
DefenseClaw splits raw device overwrite and filesystem destruction into stable IDs.
The fallback contract accepts exact shell and interpreter fork-bomb shapes; interpreter flags surrounding the payload are excluded.
ActionFacts proves supported mass-termination forms; unmodeled PowerShell parameter aliases such as ProcessName are excluded.
Git parsing proves direct core.hooksPath bypasses; global and other option-bearing config forms outside the exact grammar are excluded.
DefenseClaw semantically owns history-file mutation and HISTFILE unsetting; Bash-style clear syntax remains detection-only until shell identity is authenticated.
The fallback contract proves exact crictl and ctr execution shapes; command placement after ambiguous global options is excluded.
Normalized mutation paths cover supported writes to active executable hooks; unmodeled mutators such as sed -i are excluded.
ActionFacts proves supported privileged-account mutations; multi-member net localgroup forms outside the exact grammar are excluded.
DefenseClaw splits scheduler and service persistence across platform-stable IDs.
Normalized mutation covers selected active user and system profiles; additional upstream paths such as .zshenv and profile.d are excluded.
The active SSH path owner covers structured authorized-keys mutation.
Command-derived writes require a supported explicit mutator and active authorized-keys path; sed, Clear-Content, and New-Item forms are excluded.
The access-control owner covers proven permission and ownership mutations.
The semantic owner deliberately requires a privileged container plus a proven host-root bind; upstream's independent namespace, capability, and socket conditions are not conflated with host escape.
The semantic owner covers proven runtime-socket connects and exact container socket mounts; generic reads, environment references, and unmodeled clients are excluded.
The existing privilege owner covers sudo and bounded root-elevation discovery without adding a noisy standalone shell rule.
The fallback contract proves supported nsenter and chroot entry forms; ambiguous split chroot option values are excluded.
The active sudoers path owner covers proven mutations.
DefenseClaw retains provider and encoded-address aliases under one semantic metadata owner.
ActionFacts proves multi-target scans for supported scanners; upstream tools such as zmap and rustscan are not yet modeled.
The existing owner covers bounded sudo, find, and capability-based privilege discovery.
The active environment-file owner covers proven reads while excluding mentions and fixtures.
The active-profile owner covers selected Chromium and Firefox stores; Brave and macOS binary cookie paths are excluded.
The contextual-path owner covers supported cloud credential stores; gcloud legacy_credentials account paths are excluded.
The semantic owner proves selected AWS, GCP, Azure, Vault, and additional manager reads; unsupported batch, download, Kubernetes, and SSM forms are excluded.
DefenseClaw splits developer credential stores into stable path IDs and aliases.
The proc-environ path owner covers proven process-environment reads.
DefenseClaw splits private-key and credential-store reads into stable path owners.
The semantic owner covers fixed workload-token paths; environment-variable-expanded token paths are excluded without resolved-path proof.
Git config parsing and active .git/config overwrites cover supported executable keys; filters, diff.external, fsmonitor, config-env, and per-command -c forms are excluded.
The owner proves external git remote add and set-url mutations; raw config-based rewrites and non-external values are excluded.
Coverage is limited to active OpenClaw configuration; generic editor settings require connector and structured-content context to avoid blocking legitimate setup.
The active-state owner covers selected security-sensitive DefenseClaw state paths; arbitrary writes beneath the product directory are excluded.
A trusted old-to-new enforcement state transition is required; command text or a config-file write is not sufficient proof.
